question.text: Which of the following cartesian diagrams represent a function from X to X.

solution: X = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}. For a function from X to X, each x-value from 1 to 5 must have exactly one dot above it.
Diagram (1): the dots are (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 5), (3, 2), (4, 4). The value 3 appears twice and 5 does not appear, so it is not a function.
Diagram (2): the dots are (1, 3), (2, 3), (3, 3), (4, 3), (5, 3). Each x-value appears exactly once, so it is a function.
Diagram (3): the dots are (1, 1), (2, 2), (4, 4), (5, 5). The value 3 does not appear, so it is not a function.
Only diagram (2) represents a function from X to X.

checks.resolve_answer: Only diagram (2). It has exactly one point for each x from 1 to 5, all at y = 3. Diagram (1) has two points at x = 3 and none at x = 5. Diagram (3) has no point at x = 3.

question.text: Is every relation a function? Explain your answer and give examples.

answers.answer: No, not every relation is a function; a relation is a function only if each element of X appears exactly once as a first projection.
solution: A relation from X to Y is a function only if each element of X appears only once as a first projection.
So a relation fails if an element of X appears twice, or an element of X does not appear at all.
Example of a function: $X=\{1,2,3\}$, $R=\{(1,4),(2,5),(3,4)\}$. Each element of X appears once as a first projection, so R is a function.
Example of a non-function: $X=\{1,2,3\}$, $R=\{(1,4),(1,5),(2,6),(3,4)\}$. The element 1 appears twice (two arrows leave 1), so R is not a function.
Another non-function: $X=\{1,2,3\}$, $R=\{(1,4),(2,5)\}$. The element 3 has no arrow, so R is not a function.
Therefore not every relation is a function.

checks.resolve_answer: No. A relation is a function only if every element of X appears exactly once as a first projection. A relation fails if some element of X has no arrow or has two or more arrows. Example of a function: with X = {1, 2, 3}, R = {(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 3)} is a function. Examples that are not functions: R = {(1, 2), (1, 3), (2, 3), (3, 3)}, because 1 appears twice, and R = {(1, 2), (2, 3)}, because 3 has no image.
